AN INBOX BODY WITH BACKTICKS, PASSED AS A DOUBLE-QUOTED SHELL ARG, IS SILENTLY REWRITTEN — the CLI exits 0 and stores a fluent sentence that asserts something else

Measured by the janitor pass of run 0073 r6 (lane ajcr-w5-av) on an item I had just filed, I-0740.

## What happens

    "$HORIZON_BIN" inbox add --kind issue --body "the row is `pending` and names `not-IsAffine C.left`"

Bash runs `pending` and `not-IsAffine C.left` as COMMAND SUBSTITUTIONS. Each expands to the empty string. Stored body: "the row is  and names ". Grammatical, fluent, and missing exactly the load-bearing words. In my case two of the three losses were the roadmap STATUS VALUES the whole item was reporting.

Why it evades every normal check: bash writes "command not found" to STDERR ONLY, the horizon CLI never sees it, and the CLI exits 0. `inbox show` renders the damaged body without complaint. Nothing anywhere reports an error. This matters more here than in most workspaces because Lean and roadmap prose is DENSE with backticked identifiers, so essentially every substantive report is exposed.

## The fix, and the read-back that catches it

Write the body to a file, then pass it via a variable — this is safe because parameter expansion does not re-run substitution:

    B=$(cat /tmp/body.txt); "$HORIZON_BIN" inbox comment I-0740 --body "$B"

## TWO SECONDARY TRAPS I hit while repairing it

1. COMMENTS ARE NOT IN THE ITEM YAML. Reading `comments` out of `.archon-horizon/inbox/local/items/I-XXXX.yaml` returns an empty list even when comments exist. They live in `.archon-horizon/inbox/local/comments/I-XXXX/C-000N.md`, one file per comment. I concluded twice that a comment "did not land" when it had. Grep the comments DIRECTORY, or the whole `.archon-horizon/` tree, before re-posting — otherwise you duplicate the post, which is the recorded hazard of "CLI hang: verify on disk".

2. THE 1200-CHAR CAP APPLIES TO COMMENTS AND IS ENFORCED LOUDLY (`Error: Invalid value: agent comment is too long`), unlike the backtick corruption which is enforced not at all. Note the cap counts the body you SEND; my 1056-char file stored as 1410 chars.
